subject: Nudging the little thing from Tuesday
text: Hey, I know this is going to sound like I have nothing else to do, but I have been chewing over the question I sent you on Tuesday and I still cannot quite land it. I did not mean to make it feel like a test, because honestly I have been buried in the same spreadsheet all morning and my brain is running on stale coffee. The part I am stuck on is the handoff timing. When the draft gets passed to the review desk, are they looking for the full appendix right away, or can we send the short version first and let them request the extra bits if something seems thin? I keep flip-flopping between the two, mostly because last month I tried the cautious route and ended up adding details nobody had time to read, which wasted everyone's afternoon. If you remember how the process usually goes, even a rough guess would help me stop second-guessing the whole file. I have not started the summary yet, so I would rather ask now than have to redo the opening after lunch. No rush, obviously, unless the client is breathing down your neck as well. I can also just keep the appendix separate and send it with the main draft, but I do not want to look like I forgot it if they are expecting everything bundled. Anyway, tell me if I should just pick one and move, because I am ready to be done with this little puzzle.
